item.title: Eclipse Observables for Navigation in Cislunar Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.28669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous navigation independent of Earth-based tracking remains a challenge for spacecraft operating in cislunar space. This paper proposes onboard eclipse detection as an opportunistic measurement set to supplement the state estimation of cislunar trajectories. Penumbral and umbral entry and exit times detected from standard power telemetry are formulated as implicit zero-measurements on the boundaries of second-order shadow cones computed from planetary ephemerides. These observables are processed in an unscented Kalman filter. The event-time uncertainty that weights each measurement is derived from physical sources excluded in the spherical body model, including telemetry sampling, Earth's atmosphere, and topography/oblateness of the occulting body. The approach is demonstrated both in simulation for an $L_1$ halo orbit and with flight telemetry and orbit determination products from the CAPSTONE spacecraft during the January 2026 lunar eclipse, where umbral contacts timed directly from the power telemetry agree with the geometric contacts to within one sample interval. In both cases, hardware-free eclipse event timing shows utility in uncertainty reduction, especially as the initial solution quality is degraded.
item.dc:creator: Ian M. Down, James McElreath, Manoranjan Majji

item.title: A Catalog of Dispersive Ionospheric and Plasmaspheric Arcs from Cislunar and Lunar-surface GNSS Radio Occultations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This dataset is a catalog of 263 dispersive arcs induced by ionospheric and plasmaspheric occultation observed in GNSS signals recorded by the Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE) payload during Blue Ghost Mission 1 (BGM1), in cislunar space and on the lunar surface. Occultation arcs are identified and classified as ingress, egress or tangent by combining independently GPS and Galileo dual-frequency observables and computing the rate of the total electron content (ROT) and ROT index (ROTI), and are validated through a geometric criterion based on the grazing altitude of the tangent point. No distinction is made between the ionospheric and plasmaspheric contributions to each arc, which is treated as a single dispersive signature. For each arc, the catalog provides timing, grazing altitude, summary ROT/ROTI/$\Delta$STEC attributes, the geomagnetic activity level, and time series of leveled slant total electron content (STEC), not corrected for instrumental biases, ROT, ROTI, tangent-point position and local time. The HDF5 (Hierarchical Data Format version 5) file contains a header with dataset-wide metadata and per-class statistics, and one entry per arc. It enables rapid selection of occultation arcs for statistical studies and targeted analyses, and complements ground-based and low Earth orbit radio-occultation data during the declining phase of solar cycle 25.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Fiorina, Alex Minetto, Rebecca Ghidoni, Marco Guerra, Claudio Cesaroni, Luca Spogli, Andrea Nardin, Fabio Dovis

item.title: Optimized Bragg Grating Liquid Crystal Solar Sail
item.description: arXiv:2610.28942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have designed a thin 3-layer sun-facing diffractive Bragg reflector comprised of a chiral polymeric liquid crystal film. Using Rigorous Coupled-Wave Analysis (RCWA), the stack was optimized to maximize the transverse radiation pressure force across the wavelength band 0.47 - 1.67 micrometers. The optimized structure operates on a single polarization state of light. A two structure stack, each operating on a different state of polarization, is predicted to provide a transverse momentum transfer efficiency of 51%. This study demonstrates how a wavelength selective Bragg grating may be used both as a sunshade to scatter sunlight away from the Earth, and as a solar sail for maintaining a prescribed orbit (such as the Earth-Sun L1 point) owing to the momentum transfer efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Sai Keshav Sasanapuri (Nicole), Xiulian (Nicole), Shan, Grover A. Swartzlander Jr

item.title: An Implicit Conservative Finite Volume Scheme with Poisson Brackets for the Steady-State Transport of Galactic Cosmic Rays
item.description: arXiv:2610.30091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) pose a persistent radiation hazard to astronauts and spacecraft in the heliosphere. Modeling their transport is essential for understanding how the solar wind and heliospheric magnetic field shape their spatial distributions and energy spectra. Timely predictions require solving for the particle distribution function much faster than real time, but explicit numerical schemes are restricted by the stability limit on the time step. In this Letter, we present an implicit conservative finite-volume scheme for kinetic equations formulated with Poisson brackets. This scheme conserves particle number, maintains the total-variation-diminishing property, achieves second-order spatial accuracy, and remains stable for time steps far beyond the explicit limit, while reaching quasi-steady states in less than ~1/100 of the computational time required for the explicit scheme, as demonstrated by numerical tests. We apply this scheme to the Parker transport equation along magnetic field lines in the background solar wind during Carrington rotation 2211, where it reaches steady-state GCR distributions within 10 iterations, about 1000 times faster than the explicit scheme. The GCR proton spectrum averaged over 27 days agrees with AMS-02 measurements to within 10%. The simulation also yields a realistic radial intensity gradient and captures the Forbush decrease features associated with three stream interaction regions observed at Earth.
item.dc:creator: Weihao Liu, Igor V. Sokolov
